column1: # R15 receipt notes (tools/r15_receipt.sh 5th argument, make r15-receipt NOTES=...).
# Values are copied by hand from the qualifying run's summary.json (updated for that run before the receipt is written).

column2: L1-A activation latency (RES-1 vs SEQ), ns p50 / p99
column5: the dependency-driven path adds a fixed hop (wake, ready queue, worker pickup) that the sequential control does not have; gated budget G5 (p50 <= 50 us, p99 <= 221 us) met with large margin

column2: L1-E activation with AEGIS grant (RES-1 vs SEQ), ns p50 / p99
column5: same wake hop as L1-A; the AEGIS check itself is 22 ns p50/p99 (G6 met)

column2: L1-C scheduler, uncontended: ready-to-run ns p50 / sched wall ns p50
column5: RES-1 stamps ready when the wake enqueues and hands off to a worker thread; SEQ stamps ready when its pulse reaches the stage just before running it (its discovery time is in demand-to-ready: RES-1 64 ns vs SEQ 976 ns p50)

column2: L1-C scheduler, blocked: ready-to-run ns p50 / p99 / p99.9; demand-to-ready ns p90
column5: measured, not profiled in this campaign; the resident path re-queues a reaction released from a blocked resource, SEQ re-checks it on its next pulse; reported, not gated

column2: L1-C scheduler, priority: ready-to-run ns p50 / p99
column5: measured, not profiled in this campaign: with one worker, lower-priority ready activations wait behind higher-priority ones and that wait is counted as ready-to-run, while SEQ runs each stage in fixed order as its pulse reaches it; a real latency cost of the single-worker resident scheduler under a priority mix; reported, not gated

column2: L2 dependent wake (seat commit to dependent start), ns p50 / p99
column5: RES-1 wakes the dependent through the dependency index and a worker; SEQ runs it in the same pulse; tail not profiled in this campaign

column2: L2 end to end per GPU claim, ns p50 / p90 / p99
column5: median within 5%; the tail follows the dependent-wake tail above and the enqueue tail (p90 123969 vs 87248 ns); GPU execution on the chip clock is the same (p50 74688 vs 73504 ns)

column2: L1-G generation barrier latency, ns p99.9 (150 barriers each)
column5: single worst barrier of 150; p99 is 110.7 vs 111.4 ms; every RES-1 barrier kept production committing (G7 met)

column2: Per-trial promotion barrier latency, ns p50 / max (12 each)
column5: RES-1 keeps production committing during all 12 barriers (SEQ: 0 of 12), which costs a little barrier time; G7 p99 <= 500 ms met

column2: Package energy per episode, uJ median (not per operation)
column5: per-episode energy includes the whole episode window, during which RES-1 keeps producing (ADAPT-window rate 14476 vs 66.8 ops/s); per production operation RES-1 is lower (net 354 vs 428 uJ/op; G9 met)

column2: G10 (amendment A1, spec section 21) counts synchronization events with exactly one GPU claim in flight, so results per wake = 1 on both sides by construction; it cannot show one completion scan covering many results. A multi-claim-in-flight L2 phase (N > 1, e.g. 16; Drake Option B) is deferred to a later gate.

Host spin cost (empty completion polls per GPU result) is reported, not gated: run 2 RES-1 102.9, SEQ 106.1 (attempt 1: 77.8 vs 57.6). Both paths spin while one claim is in flight and the rate varies between runs, so it is not claimed to be small or stable.

L2 completion_publication_ns reads 0 at every percentile in both configurations (attempt 1 and run 2); the publication split of L2 end-to-end time is therefore not resolved by this rig and is not claimed.
